text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria's parliament approved a new national crest after seven years of wrangling, replacing the comunist star above the lion with a crown with 177 votes in favour, 16 against and 29 abstentions.
-- The Bulgarian National Bank said it would raise its annual main interest rate to 5.50 percent from 5.42 percent, effective Monday. @

-- Bulgaria's private Evropa insurance company said it would raise its capital to three billion levs from 300 million levs in line with new minimum capital requirements approved by parliament last month.

-- Bulgaria's Constitutional Court may rule parts of the law to open communist-era secret police files as contravining the constitution and violating civil rights of Bulgarians, Constitutional Court judge Georgi Markov said. @

-- Bulgaria's cabinet decided to use a $40 million loan extended by the World Bank to fund imports of medicines, Health Minister Petar Boyadzhiev said. Initially the loan was planned to fund critical imports of grains and foods.
-- Bulgaria will not destroy its eight SS 23 tactical warfare missiles because they are an essential part of the country's defence, Foreign Ministry officials said.
-- Bulgaria's retail prices rose by 3.4 percent in the last 10 days, National Statistics Institute figures showed. @
-- Bulgaria's forklift truck producer Balkankar Holding said it had posted some 1.9 billion lev profit for the first six months of this year.
-- Some 73 percent of the Bulgarians approve of the opening of secret police files from the communist era, a poll conducted by the National Centre for Research of Public Oppinion showed.

-- Bulgaria's parliament authorised the government to negotiate loans of 60 million Ecus from the European Investment Bank and $50 million from Kuwait's fund for Arab Economic Development to fund the reconstruction of Sofia Airport. @

-- Bulgaria's cabinet approved a bill allowing Bulgaria-registered joint ventures with less than 50 percent foreign equity to buy arable land in the country, Agriculture minister Ventsislav Varbanov said.

-- Bulgaria's government tentatively approved a draft bill to cut conscript military service to 12 months from 18 months and to nine months from one year for university graduates, effective from January 1, 1998, Defence Minister Georgi Ananiev said. @ -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 4145
